statements.proposition: This change keeps every public method and every initialization parameter of the synthesizer classes unchanged.
statements.label: CANNOT_TELL
statements.note: impact: mixed concrete evidence. No __init__ signature line changed in any diff and the methods removed from subclasses (push, monitor_connection, cleanup) are now inherited from BaseSynthesizer, so names persist. But BaseSynthesizer.push changed from sync `def push(self, text)` (a no-op stub) to `async def push(self, message)`, a literal signature change, and for sarvam/polly/openai/deepgram-style subclasses in stream=True mode the inherited push now schedules the no-op base sender instead of queueing to internal_queue (behaviour change). Whether the claim is meant to cover the abstract base stub, and whether any caller is affected, is not settled without running the code.
evidence: gh api pulls/218 patch for base_synthesizer.py: '-    def push(self, text):' replaced by '+    async def push(self, message):'

grep of +/- def lines across all patches: no __init__ lines changed; removed defs are push/monitor_connection/cleanup in elevenlabs, cartesia, smallest, azure, openai, polly, sarvam (now provided by base)
sarvam/polly/openai patches delete their own `async def push` that did internal_queue.put_nowait; base push does that only when self.stream is False
